families.stem: A data set has this frequency distribution: the value ${=m-d}$ occurs ${=k}$ times, the value ${=m}$ occurs ${=6*k}$ times and the value ${=m+d}$ occurs ${=k}$ times. Calculate the standard deviation.
solution: Deviations from the mean are $-{=d}$, $0$ and ${=d}$, so $\sum f(x-\bar{x})^2={=k}\times{=d*d}+{=k}\times{=d*d}={=2*k*d*d}$.
families.notes: Population SD (divide by sum f). Symmetric design gives mean m and SD d/2 exactly. No book question list was supplied, so parent_question_id is a placeholder.

families.stem: The table shows a grouped frequency distribution. Class ${=b0} \le x < {=b1}$: frequency ${=3*k}$. Class ${=b1} \le x < {=b2}$: frequency ${=3*k}$. Class ${=b2} \le x < {=b3}$: frequency ${=k}$. Class ${=b3} \le x < {=b4}$: frequency ${=k}$. Using the centres of the classes, calculate the standard deviation.
solution: The class centres are ${=c-w}$, ${=c}$, ${=c+w}$ and ${=c+2*w}$, with total frequency ${=8*k}$.
Variance $=\frac{{=8*k*w*w}}{{=8*k}}={=w*w}$, so the standard deviation is $\sqrt{{=w*w}}={=w}$.
families.notes: Population SD. Centres spaced w apart with offsets -1,0,1,2 and freqs 3k,3k,k,k give mean c, SD w. Placeholder parent id.

families.stem: A grouped frequency distribution has these classes: ${=b0} \le x < {=b1}$ with frequency $f$ (unknown); ${=b1} \le x < {=b2}$ with frequency ${=3*k}$; ${=b2} \le x < {=b3}$ with frequency ${=k}$; ${=b3} \le x < {=b4}$ with frequency ${=k}$. Using the class centres, the mean is ${=c}$. Find $f$ and then calculate the standard deviation.
solution: Total frequency ${=8*k}$. Deviations from the mean ${=c}$: $-{=w}$, $0$, ${=w}$, ${=2*w}$.
Variance $={=w*w}$, so the standard deviation is ${=w}$.
